summary: We are testing whether adding a lookahead window (scanning the next K candidate pieces instead of placing them in fixed order) to a skyline-based greedy polyomino packer significantly improves packing density. This is iteration 2, building on the confirmed iter-1 finding that skyline packing beats strip packing (~73 vs ~60 score). Two arms will run: the full enhanced packer (h-main, predicted ~85) and an ablation with lookahead disabled (h-ablation, predicted ~76), isolating lookahead's contribution.
key_points: h-main: Full enhanced packer with lookahead window K=n/4, roughness tiebreaker, column compaction, 3 piece orderings, and hybrid two-phase time strategy. Predicted score ~85 (probed 84.9–86.2), a ~12-point gain over iter-1 baseline (~73).

h-ablation: Same packer but with lookahead window forced to 1 (no lookahead). Predicted score ~76 (probed 71.3–81.7, high variance). The ~9-point gap between arms would confirm lookahead as the dominant mechanism.

Confirmation criteria: h-main ≥ 83 AND h-main − h-ablation ≥ 5 points confirms the lookahead hypothesis. If h-ablation scores ≥ 82, lookahead is not the key driver and secondary improvements (roughness, compaction, multi-ordering) deserve their own ablation study.

Risk factors to watch: time management on large instances (n up to 6472), validity of column compaction (cells must stay in [0,W)×[0,H)), and whether the dynamic lookahead shrinks too aggressively under load — all have explicit diagnostics in the plan.
The design cleanly isolates one mechanism (lookahead) via a single toggle (window size), with all other code paths identical between arms, making attribution straightforward.
